capabilities.target: Private repositories owned by the user
Pull request on the public repository

inputs.source: User's direct chat prompt to the desktop agent
Issue content in the public GitHub repository, authorable by anyone

elements.name: Public issue content entering agent context
Public GitHub users, including potential attackers
User's direct prompt to the agent
Pull request content published to the public repository
GitHub Personal Access Token, repo-scoped across all repositories

controls.name: Per-tool-call client approval prompt
controls.decay_rationale: The approver sees a collapsed summary rather than raw arguments by default (model_summary review), and users approve many calls per session, producing approval fatigue (SAFE-T1403, ASI09). A more persuasive or capable model can phrase requests to avoid raising suspicion.

controls.name: Least-privilege, per-repository scoped credential
controls.decay_rationale: A credential scoped to only the public repository needed for issue triage cannot reach private repository contents regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Raw-action approval view for sensitive tool calls
controls.decay_rationale: Showing the approver the full destination repository, diff, and file list rather than a collapsed summary removes the model's ability to write a misleading summary.

controls.name: Outbound content DLP scan before publishing pull requests
controls.decay_rationale: A classifier that scans PR content for patterns resembling private source files or secrets before publishing narrows the path, but reformatting or encoding of the exfiltrated content could evade a pattern-based scanner.

controls.name: Indirect prompt-injection classifier on issue content
controls.decay_rationale: A classifier flagging instruction-like content in issue bodies narrows the path, but multi-turn or obfuscated payloads can evade it and it does not scale with a stronger attacking model.

controls.name: Pinned or digest-hashed MCP server image
controls.decay_rationale: Pinning the docker image to a specific digest prevents silent substitution of a poisoned image (rug pull), independent of model behavior.

controls.name: Tamper-evident tool-call audit log
controls.decay_rationale: A log recorded outside the model's control, separate from the ephemeral approval prompt UI, provides attributable provenance regardless of model behavior.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): public issue hijacks agent into exfiltrating private repo contents via a public pull request

attack_path.note: Anyone on GitHub can open an issue on the public repo; an attacker embeds hidden instructions in the issue body that the agent reads while looking at open issues.
Following the injected instructions, the agent calls get_file_contents against the user's private repositories, using the PAT's broad repo scope.
The agent opens a pull request on the public repository containing the private repository contents, publishing them where the attacker (or anyone) can read them.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: Approval gate removed or made automatic; autonomy level raised above A1; client defaults change to auto-approve tool calls; approvals-per-session rising further.

evidence.observation: The personal access token has repo scope across every repository the user owns, public and private, enabling the broad-credential confused deputy path.
Anyone on GitHub can open issues in the public repository, giving an untrusted party a reachable entry point into the agent's context.
Approval prompts show collapsed arguments by default and users approve many calls per session, making the gate a model_summary review at high volume (consent fatigue, SAFE-T1403).
A single GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN env var is shared across all tool calls with no per-repository scoping in configuration.

recommendations.action: Scope the GitHub PAT to only the repositories this agent needs, ideally excluding private repositories entirely or using fine-grained per-repository tokens, so a hijacked agent cannot read private repository contents.
Change the approval prompt to show the raw destination, diff, and file paths for each tool call by default instead of a collapsed summary, especially for cross-repository or external-facing actions.
Add an outbound content scan on pull request bodies before publication to catch private source content or secrets before they reach a public repository.
Treat issue and comment bodies as untrusted data: apply spotlighting/delimiting and an injection classifier before allowing their content to influence tool selection.

findings.title: No attributable record of agent tool actions independent of the approval prompt (repudiation)

forecast.watch_signal: Agent autonomy or task duration increasing without any added logging or audit controls being introduced.

evidence.observation: No logging, audit trail, or action-provenance mechanism separate from the ephemeral client approval prompt is mentioned anywhere in the configuration or runtime notes.

recommendations.action: Record a tamper-evident log of every tool call, including arguments, timestamp, and approving identity, independent of the ephemeral approval prompt UI.

findings.title: Unpinned MCP server container image enables supply-chain tampering or rug-pull substitution (ASI04)

forecast.watch_signal: Docker image resolves to a different digest between runs; unexpected changes to tool names, descriptions, or schemas exposed by the server.

evidence.observation: The docker run command references 'ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server' with no digest or version tag, so it resolves to whatever image the registry currently serves under that reference.

recommendations.action: Pin the MCP server container to a specific image digest and verify it before each run, rather than relying on an implicit 'latest' resolution.

stride_coverage.rationale: The agent runs as a local desktop process invoked directly by the user on their own machine; there is no remote peer that could assume the agent's identity in this single-user design.
Artifacts do not describe any server-side logging within the github-mcp-server container itself, separate from client-side approval prompts.
No information on resource limits, timeouts, or sandboxing constraints for the docker container running the MCP server is provided.
This inbound flow carries attacker-authored issue text into the agent; it carries no confidential data whose disclosure in transit would matter.
Artifacts do not state any rate limit on how many issues can be opened or processed by the agent per session.
Attribution of GitHub issue authorship is governed by GitHub's own platform identity system, outside this agent design's control plane.
Artifacts do not describe any protection against post-creation modification of pull request content once published.
No limits on pull request creation frequency or size are stated in the artifacts.
Only a read capability (get_file_contents) against private repositories is declared in this design; no write capability to private repos exists for the agent to exploit.
No information on GitHub API rate limits or quota consumption for get_file_contents calls is provided.
No limits on the number or size of pull requests created per session against the public repository are stated.
No capability in this design allows the agent to modify, rotate, or reconfigure its own credentials; the PAT is supplied externally via environment variable at launch.
Artifacts do not show whether the agent or MCP server could be induced to reflect or disclose the raw PAT value itself, separate from the data it grants access to.
The PAT is a static long-lived credential rather than a shared, rate-limited resource, so its exhaustion is not a meaningful denial-of-service vector here.

rating.rationale: Inherent risk is critical because an untrusted GitHub issue (anyone can open one) can reach a broadly-scoped credential that both reads private repository contents and publishes to a public pull request: the TC1 lethal trifecta (ASI01 goal hijack feeding ASI02 tool misuse through an ASI03 confused-deputy credential). The only declared control is a per-call approval prompt that shows a collapsed, model-generated summary at high approval volume (ASI09 consent fatigue), which the rubric credits only one tier, leaving residual at high. An unpinned MCP server container image (ASI04) independently sits at high because no control restores that missing property. The forecast reaches critical because the approval gate is both model-summary (decays under model_upgrade) and removable under autonomy_increase or control_removal, at which point the full inherent critical risk is unmitigated.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration shown in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No system prompt or full agent instructions were provided; only the MCP server configuration and runtime notes were available, so the autonomy level and approval workflow are inferred from documentation at medium confidence.

No source code or IaC was provided for the client application; the approval prompt's exact behavior (collapsed arguments, approval volume) is taken as described rather than verified against the implementation.
